task_description: Install the battery module in the rear compartment, connect to the high-voltage harness, and verify torque on fasteners.
generated_work_instruction:
**Safety Precautions:**
- Isolate vehicle electrical system (Lockout/Tagout) and verify 0V state before handling components.
- Wear Class 0 high-voltage (HV) insulated gloves with leather protectors, safety glasses, and ESD/insulated safety shoes.

**Required Tools & Equipment:**
- Insulated battery lifting hoist/fixture
- Calibrated digital torque wrench (with insulated socket)
- Digital multimeter / HV voltage tester
- Torque witness paint marker and MES/logbook terminal

**Step-by-Step Procedure:**
1. Verify vehicle power is completely off, confirm service disconnect plug is removed, and put on HV PPE.
2. Inspect the rear compartment mounting tray and HV harness connector pins for debris or damage.
3. Use the insulated lifting hoist to lower and seat the battery module flush onto the rear compartment locating pins.
4. Thread all mounting fasteners by hand to prevent cross-threading, then tighten in the specified cross-pattern sequence using a calibrated digital torque wrench to factory torque values.
5. Align and insert the high-voltage harness connector until an audible click is heard, then push the red Connector Position Assurance (CPA) secondary lock fully forward.
6. Apply torque witness marks to each fastener and record fastener torque values and serial numbers in the production logbook.

**Acceptance Criteria & Quality Check:**
- Battery module sits flush against all mounting pads with zero cable pinch points.
- All fasteners meet target torque specification (recorded in MES/logbook) and have witness marks applied.
- HV harness primary latch and CPA secondary lock are fully engaged with zero tug movement.

task_description: Calibrate the ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems) radar sensors on the front bumper using factory alignment targets.
generated_work_instruction:
**Safety Precautions:**
- Ensure vehicle is parked in the designated ADAS calibration bay with parking brake engaged and wheel chocks installed.
- Keep laser alignment line-of-sight clear and avoid staring directly into alignment lasers.

**Required Tools & Equipment:**
- OEM ADAS calibration frame and corner reflector / radar alignment target board
- Laser wheel-alignment / centerline measurement rig
- Tire pressure gauge and vehicle ballast weights (if specified)
- OEM diagnostic scan tool connected via OBD-II

**Step-by-Step Procedure:**
1. Position the vehicle on a level calibration floor, verify tire pressures match placard specifications, and confirm front bumper fascia is clean and undamaged.
2. Establish the vehicle thrust line and geometric centerline using the laser alignment rig.
3. Place the factory radar alignment target at the exact longitudinal distance, lateral offset, and height specified for the new model in front of the bumper radar sensor.
4. Clear the radar field of view of all metallic objects, tools, and personnel within the calibration cone.
5. Connect the OEM diagnostic tool to the OBD-II port, switch ignition to ON (engine/propulsion OFF), and launch the Front Radar Static Calibration routine.
6. Follow on-screen prompts until calibration completes, clear any temporary DTCs, and save the calibration certificate to the vehicle build record.

**Acceptance Criteria & Quality Check:**
- Horizontal and vertical radar misalignment angles fall within factory tolerance (+/- 0.5 deg or model spec).
- Diagnostic tool reports 'Calibration Successful' with zero active ADAS fault codes.

task_description: Apply anti-corrosion sealant to all exposed welds on the door panels before painting.
generated_work_instruction:
**Safety Precautions:**
- Work in a ventilated booth/station and wear nitrile gloves, safety glasses, and an approved organic-vapor respirator if required by SDS.
- Keep solvent cleaners away from ignition sources.

**Required Tools & Equipment:**
- Lint-free wipes and approved degreaser / surface prep solvent
- Pneumatic or manual seam-sealer applicator gun with approved anti-corrosion sealant cartridge
- Nylon spreader / brush tool
- Wet-film thickness gauge and inspection light

**Step-by-Step Procedure:**
1. Inspect door panel hem flanges and weld seams for weld spatter, burrs, oil, or dust.
2. Wipe all exposed welds and adjacent metal surfaces using lint-free cloths dampened with approved surface cleaner, then allow to flash dry completely.
3. Dispense a continuous, uniform bead of approved anti-corrosion sealant along every exposed weld seam and joint overlap, keeping sealant out of drain holes.
4. Tool or brush the sealant bead immediately where required to wet the weld edges and eliminate air pockets or pinholes.
5. Place the door panel on the curing rack and allow the specified flash/curing time before transferring to the paint booth.
6. Perform a visual 360-degree seam inspection under bright lighting prior to releasing the panel.

**Acceptance Criteria & Quality Check:**
- 100% continuous sealant coverage over all exposed welds with no gaps, skips, air bubbles, or bridged drain holes.
- Sealant cured properly and free of surface contamination prior to paint entry.

task_description: Perform leak test on coolant system after radiator installation. Record pressure readings and verify against specifications.
generated_work_instruction:
**Safety Precautions:**
- Never open a pressurized or hot cooling system; wear safety goggles and chemical-resistant gloves.
- Stand clear of radiator hoses and relief valves while pressurizing the system.

**Required Tools & Equipment:**
- Calibrated cooling system pressure tester kit with model-specific reservoir adapter cap
- Timer / stopwatch
- Inspection mirror and UV/inspection flashlight
- Shop-floor quality logsheet / MES terminal

**Step-by-Step Procedure:**
1. Confirm radiator, clamps, drain plug, and coolant hoses are fully installed and the system is at ambient temperature.
2. Attach the calibrated pressure tester adapter securely to the coolant expansion tank / radiator neck.
3. Pump/pressurize the cooling system gradually to the factory test pressure specification (do not exceed maximum rated cap pressure).
4. Record the initial stabilized pressure reading and start the hold timer for the required test duration (e.g., 2–5 minutes per engineering spec).
5. Visually inspect the radiator core, hose junctions, clamps, water pump housing, and drain plug for any weeping, seepage, or air hiss.
6. Record the final pressure reading at the end of the hold period, compare pressure drop against engineering specifications, safely depressurize via the relief valve, and remove the adapter.

**Acceptance Criteria & Quality Check:**
- Pressure drop over the test hold duration is within factory maximum allowable decay (0 psi / within tolerance) with zero visible leaks.
- Initial pressure, final pressure, hold duration, and pass/fail status recorded in the build record.

task_description: Program the infotainment ECU with the latest software package and validate connectivity with dashboard display.
generated_work_instruction:
**Safety Precautions:**
- Connect an approved 12V battery maintainer/power supply before flashing to prevent low-voltage ECU bricking.
- Observe ESD precautions when handling diagnostic cables and connectors.

**Required Tools & Equipment:**
- Regulated 12V automotive programming power supply
- OEM VCI (Vehicle Communication Interface) / OBD-II diagnostic programming terminal with verified latest software package
- Test smartphone / test media source (USB/Bluetooth) for functional validation

**Step-by-Step Procedure:**
1. Connect the regulated 12V power supply to the vehicle auxiliary battery terminals and verify stable voltage (13.2V–13.8V).
2. Plug the OEM VCI diagnostic connector into the vehicle OBD-II port, turn vehicle ignition to Accessory/ON mode, and verify vehicle VIN communication.
3. Select the Infotainment Head Unit (IVI ECU), verify current hardware part number compatibility, and initiate flashing with the latest approved software release package.
4. Wait without interrupting power or opening/closing doors until programming reaches 100% and the ECU performs its automatic hard reset.
5. Verify the dashboard center display boots cleanly, confirm the updated software version string on the system info screen, and test touch response, instrument cluster CAN sync, audio output, and Bluetooth/USB connectivity.
6. Run a post-flash DTC scan, clear communication reset codes, log software version to MES, and disconnect VCI and power supply.

**Acceptance Criteria & Quality Check:**
- Infotainment ECU reports exact target software version number with zero active DTCs.
- Dashboard display renders without artifacts, responds to touch/steering-wheel controls, and passes audio/connectivity checks.
